summary: Introductory security intake focused on whether Redwood Hosted or Dedicated/Private fits Grayhaven's regulatory and ops constraints. Main concerns: KMS / BYOK, SSO/SAML integration, RBAC model, audit log retention, and data residency. Decided to run a technical deep dive and share SOC2/ISO artifacts.
topics: KMS/BYOK, SSO/SAML, RBAC, audit logs and retention, data residency, hosted vs dedicated vs private tradeoffs, timeline and pilot scope
transcript:
[00:00] Maya (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick roll call, I'll hand to Arjun after a one minute overview.
[00:12] Evan (Grayhaven Head of Security): Hey, Evan here. We run payments middleware and a customer support AI feature, so really focusing on data controls.
[00:20] Priya (Platform Eng): Priya, platform. We're evaluating hosted first but have strong BYOK and residency asks.
[00:28] Maya: Cool. So agenda — security posture, infra options (hosted/dedicated/private), and next steps. Arjun?
[00:36] Arjun (Redwood SE): Thanks. Quick on tech — Redwood provides Hosted API, Dedicated reserved pools, and Private (VPC/on-prem). For security we support customer-managed KMS, SSO via SAML, RBAC, and audit logs.
[00:50] Tom (DevOps): For KMS, do you support external HSMs or only cloud KMS? We need FIPS-validated HSM for keys.
[00:59] Arjun: We integrate with AWS KMS, GCP KMS, and customers can bring keys via external KMS/HSM brokers in our Private deployment — there are some network constraints though. We'll share HSM integration docs.
[01:15] Evan: Also retention — our policy is 90 days for raw logs, seven years for audit trail. Can you commit to retention windows and exportability?
[01:24] Lena (CSM): We can set retention policies per account; for Hosted we offer configurable retention and exports. For Private, you control storage.
[01:35] Maya: Important note — Hosted team-run logs are available via the Console and via syslog/export. For enterprise, we can negotiate long-term log retainment in Dedicated contracts.
[01:47] Priya: SSO — we're SAML IdP (Okta). How's group sync and SCIM? We need role sync for service accounts.
[01:56] Arjun: SAML SSO is supported; SCIM provisioning is available to enterprise customers. RBAC supports granular roles and custom roles. There is a small caveat with service-to-service tokens — those are managed via our tokens system which can be scoped to projects and rotated.
[02:15] Tom: Can we rotate keys from our KMS and have Redwood acknowledge revocation quickly?
[02:21] Arjun: On Private/Dedicated we can wire up key rotation via KMS events; hosted has rotation windows — we'll detail TTLs. There can be a short cache window on active model KV cache — we call it probably the kevee cache in some docs — it persists until process cold start, so immediate revocation may need a short TTL.
[02:45] Evan: Hmm, that cache worry is critical. If keys are revoked, we need guarantee tokens can't be used, and model context cached in memory should not leak data.
[02:54] Arjun: Absolutely. We have a mechanism to flush KV cache on key rollover for Dedicated and Private. Hosted can be configured to flush but requires coordination with infra ops; we'll note that as an item.
[03:08] Priya: Encryption at rest — do you encrypt embeddings and generated artifacts?
[03:13] Arjun: Yes, TLS in transit and AES-256 at rest. With customer-managed keys, you control the root keys. Some artifacts like metadata are stored in our control plane; for Private deployments, control plane can be customer self-hosted.
[03:30] Maya: Quick qualification — what's your timeline and success criteria?
[03:35] Evan: Timeline is Q3 pilot, production by Q1 next year. Success criteria: latency under 200ms p50 for support workflows, SOC2 or ISO evidence in evaluation, and contractual BYOK.
[03:48] Tom: Also cost. Hosted is attractive but we need predictable throughput for peak events.
[03:54] Arjun: For predictable throughput we recommend Dedicated; it gives reserved GPU pools and SLOs. Hosted has autoscale, but Dedicated gives throughput guarantees and private tenancy.
[04:07] Priya: Data residency — some PII derived from inputs must remain in EU. Can you guarantee regional hosting?
[04:14] Arjun: Yes, we have EU regions and can pin workloads regionally. Private can run in a customer's VPC in-region. We'll send the region mapping doc.
[04:25] Evan: Audit logs — what do you log? Who can access them? Retention, immutability?
[04:31] Lena: Audit logs include API calls, model version changes, user access, and admin actions. Access can be restricted via RBAC and auditor roles; immutability is supported via append-only storage for Dedicated/Private.
[04:46] Sofia (Legal): From a legal standpoint we need a copy of the SOC2 report and a section on subprocessor list and DPA clauses.
[04:55] Maya: We'll share SOC2 Type II and ISO-27001 certificates, plus the current subprocessor list and template DPA.
[05:03] Evan: Any red-team or pen-test history?
[05:07] Arjun: We do regular third-party pen tests; summary reports are in the security pack.
[05:12] Priya: One technical: how does fallback work if Dedicated pool hits capacity? We need graceful degradation path, not an outage.
[05:20] Arjun: Smart routing can fallback to compatible model variants or hosted capacity depending on policy. For mission-critical flows, we recommend a hot standby Dedicated pool or cross-region failover.
[05:34] Tom: For pilot, can you run a small Dedicated pool with burst to hosted?
[05:38] Maya: Yes, that's a common pattern — commit to base Dedicated and allow bursting to Hosted. We'll provide cost scenarios.
[05:47] Evan: Regarding RBAC, can roles be time-limited for contractors?
[05:51] Arjun: Yes, expiring roles and time-bound access are supported via SSO provisioning. We can also integrate with your access review tooling.
[06:02] Priya: Is there a way to red-team prompts or scrub PII before sending to model? We already have a preprocessor.
[06:09] Arjun: We support prefix filtering and pre-send hooks in Dedicated/Private where you can run your preprocessor in-path; for Hosted we offer a credentials scrubber but for full control Private is recommended.
[06:24] Evan: What's the SLA for logs and for API availability?
[06:29] Maya: Hosted SLA is 99.9 for availability for paid tiers; Dedicated SLA options go to 99.95 depending on contract. Log retention SLA varies by package.
[06:40] Sofia: Regarding eDiscovery and legal holds — can you export all data for a tenant in a searchable format?
[06:46] Lena: Yes, exports include full request/response archives and can be delivered via secure object storage export. We'll outline formats.
[06:55] Tom: Any known gotchas with Kubernetes networking for Private?
[07:00] Arjun: Private deployments can be managed or self-hosted; in either case we require certain CNI configs and open ports. We'll share a runbook.
[07:10] Priya: Also curious about model version pinning and rollbacks — we need stable behavior for customer support scripts.
[07:17] Arjun: You can pin model versions per route and perform canary rollouts; automatic fallback to previous version is supported if regressions are detected.
[07:29] Evan: Great. For the next steps, we need the SOC2 pack, a diagram for Private deployment, and an initial benchmark plan.
[07:36] Maya: We'll send those today/tomorrow. Arjun will run the technical deep dive next week. Any other questions?
[07:42] Sofia: One last — do you allow contractual obligations around subprocessor disclosure windows?
[07:48] Maya: Yes, we can commit to 30-day notice for major subprocessor changes in the DPA; we'll surface the legal template.
[07:56] Evan: Thanks, that covers it.
[08:00] Maya: Thanks everyone. We'll follow up with the pack and book the deep dive.
[08:05] [call ends]
